title: Air Astana Flight 1388
subtitle: Alverca → Beja (bound for Minsk)
note: A reconstruction of a real accident in which nobody died. The aircraft rolled far more than its path can show: the recorded attitude is not published.
summary: An Air Astana Embraer 190 on a positioning flight after heavy maintenance at Alverca, near Lisbon, bound for Almaty via Minsk, with three pilots and three Air Astana technicians aboard.
During the maintenance the aileron control cables of both wings had been installed reversed. From take-off in low cloud at 13:31 the aircraft did not respond normally and rolled abnormally.

In direct mode, by trial and error, the crew regained partial control, found clearer weather to the east and, escorted by two Portuguese Air Force F-16s, landed at Beja on the third approach at 15:27.

card.title: Air Astana Flight 1388
lines: 11 November 2018 · Embraer 190-100LR P4-KCJ, a positioning flight from Alverca to Almaty via Minsk.

The aileron control cables of both wings had been installed reversed during heavy maintenance, and the checks after it did not find it. For almost two hours the crew flew an aircraft that answered their roll inputs the wrong way.
They landed at Beja at 15:27. Of the six people aboard, one passenger was injured. The flight loads damaged the airframe: skin panels, the wing leading edges and the wing dihedral.

The investigation found the most probable cause in the improper aileron cable installation and the inadequate independent inspection after it, with contributing factors at the maintenance organisation, the manufacturer, the operator, the supervising authorities and in the crew's pre-flight checks.
Reconstruction from the final report of Portugal's GPIAAF (08/ACCID/2018, 2020) and published multilateration data.
